subject: Service-chain attestation request — SIG/CAIQ evidence for third-party mapping
messages:
From: Liam Porter <liam.porter@medsource.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@healthex.com
Cc: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@healthex.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: SIG/CAIQ + subprocessor attestation for HealthEx integration

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the quick connect during onboarding. As part of our vendor intake we need a standard SIG/CAIQ bundle and a short attestation that lists your active subprocessors, their geographic residency, and whether any have access to unredacted customer data or KMS key material. Specific asks: 

- Completed SIG/CAIQ (v3) answers or CAIQ compendium where applicable.
- A machine-readable subprocessor roster (.xlsx preferred) with columns: service name, provider, primary region, onshore/offshore flag, has_kms_access (yes/no), purpose.
- KMS/residency statement for any provider that can access encryption keys or key material.
- Any SOC 2 references or links to reports (if available) and the SOC scope.

Target timeline is two weeks from today (2026-06-24). Please let me know if you need additional clarification on scope or format — we can accept a SIG-Lite if that reduces lift, but procurement will flag missing KMS/residency items.

Best,
Liam Porter
Security & Risk, MedSource.ai
liam.porter@medsource.ai

Attachment: sample_evidence_checklist.csv (reference)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam Porter <liam.porter@medsource.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SIG/CAIQ + subprocessor attestation for HealthEx integration

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear checklist. We're happy to provide what you need. Quick clarifications so we scope correctly: 

1) SIG scope: do you require SIG v3 full answers or is a SIG-Lite / CAIQ adequate for procurement acceptance?
2) Subprocessor roster: confirm you want active *serving* subprocessors (inference, telemetry, KMS providers) and not short-lived contractors; we'll include contracted vendors with any production access.
3) Residency detail: do you need ISO timestamps (e.g., first deploy date) or just region and onshore/offshore designation?

Plan on our side: Marissa will assemble the technical evidence (KMS/residency and runtime dependency provenance) and I will pull the roster and business attestations. Ben, can you flag any contractual redlines if we attach SOC 2 excerpts or NDA-protected artifacts?

If SIG v3 full is required we may ask for a short extension (3 days) beyond your two-week window to ensure legal review for some attachments. Otherwise, we'll aim for 2026-06-24.

Thanks — sending an initial roster snapshot by end of day tomorrow.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Head of Compliance, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com
REDWOOD INFERENCE

---
Note: Ben/Marissa — I'm assigning you both for evidence pulls and legal checks.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-11T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Service-chain attestation request — SIG/CAIQ evidence for third-party mapping

Adding a quick note: Marissa, when you pull the KMS/residency artifacts please mark anything that references customer-specific keys as 'legal-review' — we should not publish full key identifiers or KMS ARNs in a shared folder. SOC 2: we have an excerpt (scope: authentication, storage, and data processing) that procurement can reference; full report is available under NDA. I'll start a redaction pass on SOC excerpts and prepare a short cover letter explaining scope and limitations.

Also, in the roster include a column "controls_managed_by_redwood" (yes/no) to make clear which responsibilities remain ours for operational controls.

Ben
Sr. Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Liam Porter <liam.porter@medsource.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@healthex.com, Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@healthex.com>
Date: 2026-06-12T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Service-chain attestation request — SIG/CAIQ evidence for third-party mapping

Thanks — that sounds good. Procurement is fine with a SIG-Lite plus the CAIQ compendium and the machine-readable roster, provided the KMS/residency items are explicit. We accept redacted SOC 2 excerpts with an NDA; please put a short cover note explaining the redaction and the SOC scope (auth, storage, processing).

For timelines: extension accepted — new target of 2026-06-27 for full artifacts including redacted SOC excerpts and KMS residency statement. Can you also attach a short CSV that maps each subprocessor to the Redwood service component (for example: "inference-serving:v1 -> GPU provider X"), that helps our procurement automation.

I'll follow up with a DocuSign NDA link for the SOC if needed. HubSpot deal id is DEAL-7421.

Appreciate the quick coordination.

Best,
Liam
